title: Percentile alarms econ tradeoff playbook (draft)
summary: Working playbook draft tying percentile alarm thresholds (p50/p90/p95/p99) to incremental cost impact and remediation guidance for console alerting rules.
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook to help product, SRE, and Console teams choose percentile alarm thresholds that balance user-facing latency risk against incremental infra cost. The focus is on RLHF-style chat workloads and short-turn generation (<= 512 tokens) where token/TTR sensitivity and KV-cache hit dynamics dominate.

Goals:
- Provide pragmatic threshold guidance for p50/p90/p95/p99 alarms and associated cost delta expectations.
- Offer simple text charts and heuristics for communicating tradeoffs to PMs and sales engineering.
- Capture remediation playbook snippets (auto-scaling vs fallback model vs alert routing) for runbooks.

Quick takeaways (high level):
- Tight p50 alarms (aggressive) -> low user-visible penalty but high noise and potentially high autoscaling churn cost. Expect 5–12% incremental cost for a p50 alarm aggressively configured to trigger on 10% upward drift.
- p95/p99 focus reduces noise; p99 alerts catch tail regressions that often correlate with model/kv cache thrash and can be 20–40% more expensive to remediate per incident if runbook triggers capacity expansion.
- For most customers, default console recommendation should be: p90 warning, p95 alert, p99 pager.

Textual cost-latency tradeoff sketches (approximate, for communication only):
Legend: latency percentiles on x-axis, relative infra cost on y-axis (baseline cost = 1.0 at steady-state p90).

Curve A: Conservative (low-noise) thresholds
p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99
0.6  0.8  1.0  1.15  1.4  (relative cost)
Notes: Minimal autoscale churn, latency slack used for batching. Good default for mid-tier customers.

Curve B: Aggressive (tight p50) thresholds
p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99
1.05 1.0  1.0  1.15  1.3
Notes: p50 configured to notify on small upward shifts. Relative cost bump driven by early scaling and human triage overhead.

Curve C: Tail-sensitive posture
p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99
0.6  0.85 1.0  1.25  1.8
Notes: Investment in tail detection: more cost allocated to tail mitigations (redundant capacity, fast fallbacks).

Simple numeric vignette (example customer):
- Baseline QPS: 1200, median latency: 120ms, p95: 360ms, daily tokens: 5M.
- Action: move from p95-alert -> p90-warning + p95-alert. Observed response: autoscale incidents reduced by 38%, token-cost change ~+3% (slight increased steady-state batch inefficiency).
- Counter: moving to p50-alert increased incident churn by 2.2x and raised monthly infra + human ops cost by ~9%.

Alarm rule anatomy (console-focused):
- Metric: per-tenant request latency (session-sliced) computed over 1m rolling windows.
- Window & aggregation: 1m rollup, percentile aggregator (hdr histogram).
- Conditions: p95 > 400ms for 3/5 consecutive windows -> alert; p99 > 700ms -> pager.
- Suppression: outlier-suppression using moving-median baseline and scheduled blackout for maintenance windows.

Remediation options and approximate cost impact (notes):
- Increase replica pool (horizontal scaling): fast, 2–10% cost increase per incident depending on immediate scale factor.
- Route to cheaper quantized variant (fallback): low-latency fix with quality tradeoff; cost delta small but product risk higher.
- Enable pre-warmed slots (keep N GPUs warm for critical tenants): predictable cost uplift (flat monthly premium) but reduces incident remediation spend.

Text chart: incident-to-cost mapping (bins)
Bin name | incident rate | cost per incident (infra + ops)
small-noise | 0.02/day | $90
moderate | 0.1/day | $450
major-tail | 0.005/day | $2,400

Console UX guidance (what to show customers):
- For each percentile alarm, show 3 numbers: expected false-positive rate (weekly), expected infra delta (monthly $), and remediation playbook.
- Provide a slider: `risk appetite` (conservative <-> aggressive) which maps to presets: conservative (p95/p99), balanced (p90/p95/p99), aggressive (p50/p90/p95).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need empirical mapping from p95 -> autoscale-trigger frequency across 10 real customer workloads. Ticket: JIRA-RENO-291.
- How does KV-cache hit rate interact with percentile alarms? Propose an experiment that toggles cache TTLs and measures p99 sensitivity (notes in linked PR).
- Should we expose a cost-estimator in the console for predicted monthly delta if a customer switches posture? Implementation depends on pricing model; start with token-based estimate.

Runbook snippet (quick):
1) Alert fires (p99 > threshold) -> run preflight checks: routing errors, 5xx, container OOMs, cache miss rate.
2) If infra saturation suspected (GPU util > 90%), trigger scale-up policy (documented HPA).
3) If tail-only for specific tenant: temporarily reduce model variant or limit concurrency.
4) Post-incident: create incident note with timeline and cost estimate (console should auto-populate).

References and cross-links:
- See CONFLUENCE-8342 for baseline benchmark methodology.
- Linked bench PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412 (contains synthetic workloads used for the example).
- Slack thread: #observability-alerting (thread id in metadata).

Notes to self / collaboration cues:
- This doc intentionally lightweight; want to bake into console as guided wizard.
- Maya: can you add synthetic run results for KV cache TTL sweep?
- Ethan: help draft the console slider UI wording and cost calculation stub.

Status: draft — please mark comments inline or in the linked Confluence doc.
